class.name: GodotChorus

method.name: load_model
method.description: Admits an asynchronous load using the current configuration. Check [member ChorusLoadResult.accepted] and correlate its load ID with [signal GodotChorus.model_loaded] or [signal GodotChorus.model_load_failed]. Acceptance immediately closes inference admission until readiness is published. Only one load can be outstanding. Rejection leaves the existing engine intact and emits no load signals; accepted replacement does not restore the old engine on failure.

method.name: cancel_load
method.description: Requests cooperative cancellation of the identified load without waiting for cleanup. Returns true when cancellation is accepted, or false for an unknown, drained or already-failed load. Accepted cancellation produces [signal GodotChorus.model_load_failed] with [constant GodotChorus.ERR_CANCELLED] after cleanup. An indivisible provider operation may delay that signal.

method.name: stop_all
method.description: Stops work and unloads the engine. This call blocks until engine and load cleanup finish. Accepted requests and an outstanding load receive their terminal signals during later node processing; keep processing enabled to receive them.

method.name: is_loaded
method.description: Returns whether an initialized engine is currently ready to accept work. False while loading, after stopping, or after an engine-wide failure. A progress fraction is not a readiness check.

method.name: supports_embeddings
method.description: Returns whether the currently loaded engine supports embeddings. False when no engine is ready. Load an embedding-capable model before calling [method GodotChorus.embed].

method.name: generate
method.description: Submits a frozen generation request and returns its immediate admission result. An empty session uses a raw prompt without history. A nonempty session admits a new chat turn and reserves that session until terminal delivery. Success emits [signal GodotChorus.generation_complete]; failure emits [signal GodotChorus.generation_error]. A failed or cancelled new turn removes its pending user message.

method.name: generate_batch
method.description: Submits requests in array order and returns one admission result per input at the same index. Admission is not atomic: some requests may be accepted while others are rejected. Requests for the same occupied session are rejected with [constant GodotChorus.ERR_SESSION_BUSY]. Each accepted item has its own terminal signal.

method.name: regenerate
method.description: Replaces the latest assistant reply in a session. The request must have a nonempty session, empty content, and history ending in an assistant message. Use [method ChorusRequest.regeneration] to create it. Success preserves the reply identity; cancellation or failure restores the previous reply. Completion and errors use the normal generation signals.

method.name: embed
method.description: Submits text for embedding without reading or changing history. A nonempty session acts as a correlation and occupancy key. Success emits [signal GodotChorus.embedding_complete]; failure emits [signal GodotChorus.generation_error]. Check the admission result before waiting.

method.name: embed_batch
method.description: Submits embedding requests in array order. Returns one independent admission result per input; a rejection does not roll back accepted items. Each accepted item receives its own embedding completion or error signal.

method.name: cancel_request
method.description: Requests cancellation of an active request. Returns false if the ID is not active. A successfully cancelled request remains active, and its session remains occupied, until its terminal signal is delivered.

method.name: is_request_active
method.description: Returns whether the request still has an undelivered terminal result. Work may already have finished on a worker thread while this remains true.

method.name: active_request_for_session
method.description: Returns the request ID occupying the session, or [code]-1[/code] if none. Prompt previews and token counts do not occupy sessions.

method.name: import_conversation_history
method.description: Replaces stored history for a nonempty session and resets its recorded turn outcome. Message IDs must be nonnegative and unique within the array; messages and roles must be valid. Empty history is allowed. An occupied session returns [constant GodotChorus.ERR_SESSION_BUSY]. Input resources are copied, and invalid input leaves existing history unchanged.

method.name: export_conversation_history
method.description: Returns copies of stored messages in conversation order. Unknown sessions return an empty array. Changing the returned resources does not change stored history. Prompt fitting does not remove messages from this export.

method.name: clear_conversation_history
method.description: Removes the session history and recorded turn outcome. Unknown sessions succeed. An occupied session returns [constant GodotChorus.ERR_SESSION_BUSY] without changing history.

method.name: edit_message
method.description: Changes the content of an existing message while preserving its identity and role. An unknown session or message returns [constant GodotChorus.ERR_INVALID_REQUEST]; an occupied session returns [constant GodotChorus.ERR_SESSION_BUSY].

method.name: list_conversations
method.description: Returns stored session names, including sessions with imported empty history. The order is unspecified.

method.name: reset_context
method.description: Removes all stored conversations and recorded turn outcomes without unloading the engine. Returns [constant GodotChorus.ERR_SESSION_BUSY] without changing history if any session is occupied.

method.name: last_turn_outcome
method.description: Returns the most recently recorded generation outcome for the session. Unknown sessions and sessions without a recorded turn return [constant GodotChorus.TURN_NONE].

method.name: render_prompt
method.description: Submits a read-only preview of a frozen request, history and defaults snapshot. Does not occupy a session, generate tokens, or change history or turn outcomes. Success emits [signal GodotChorus.prompt_rendered]; validation and fitting errors emit [signal GodotChorus.generation_error]. For deterministic templates, the same snapshot produces the same fitted prompt as generation.

method.name: count_message_tokens
method.description: Counts literal content asynchronously without occupying a session. No beginning-of-sequence or end-of-sequence tokens are added, and control-token spellings remain literal text. Counts exclude roles, templates and response reservation, so they are not additive formatted prompt costs. Success emits [signal GodotChorus.message_token_counted]; failure emits [signal GodotChorus.generation_error].

method.name: supports_message_token_counting
method.description: Returns whether the ready engine supports literal message token counting. False when no engine is ready.

method.name: similarity_cos
method.description: Returns cosine similarity of two equal-length, nonempty vectors. Zero-length norms return [code]0.0[/code]. Empty arrays or mismatched lengths report a Godot error and return [code]0.0[/code]. No loaded model is required.

members.member: Path to a loose GGUF file. Accepts absolute filesystem paths and Godot [code]res://[/code] or [code]user://[/code] paths. Models inside a PCK must first be extracted to the filesystem. The Echo provider does not require a path. Changes apply to the next accepted load.

Read-only per-request context capacity of the ready model, in tokens. Returns zero when no engine is ready or the provider does not report a capacity. This is effective metadata, not the requested load setting.
Read-only outstanding load identity until its terminal is delivered, or [code]-1[/code] when no load is outstanding.
Provider used by the next accepted model load. Selecting a provider updates its dynamic load options in the Inspector but does not replace a running engine.
Whether the next load uses this node's [member GodotChorus.log_level] instead of the project setting [code]chorus/logging/min_level[/code].

Minimum diagnostic severity for the next load when [member GodotChorus.override_log_level] is enabled. Uses [enum GodotChorus.LogLevelCode]; [constant GodotChorus.LOG_OFF] disables records. Without an override, the project setting supplies the threshold.

signal.name: model_load_progress
signal.description: Reports progress for an accepted load. The model ID is the admission-time logical model label, not a request ID. The fraction is meaningful only when [param has_fraction] is true, and describes the reported phase, not overall progress. Even a completed weight fraction is not readiness.

signal.name: model_loaded
signal.description: Terminal success for an accepted load. The engine is published as ready before delivery. Correlate [param load_id] with the admission result. Earlier callbacks in the same event batch can stop or replace the engine, so check [method GodotChorus.is_loaded] before submitting new work.

signal.name: model_load_failed
signal.description: Terminal failure for an accepted load, including cancellation after cleanup. The error code uses [enum GodotChorus.ErrorCode]. A failed replacement does not restore the previous engine.

signal.name: prompt_rendered
signal.description: Terminal success for a prompt preview. The text is the fitted prompt; omitted IDs identify stored messages excluded from this prompt only. Stored history remains unchanged.

signal.name: message_token_counted
signal.description: Terminal success for literal-content token counting. Correlate the request ID with the result from [method GodotChorus.count_message_tokens].

signal.name: token_generated
signal.description: Incremental visible text for a streaming generation request. A chunk need not correspond to one model token. The session is empty for stateless work. The final completion includes the full visible text.

signal.name: reasoning_token_generated
signal.description: Incremental reasoning text, separate from visible content, for a streaming request with reasoning exposure enabled. The final completion includes the full exposed reasoning.

signal.name: generation_complete
signal.description: Terminal generation success with full visible content and exposed reasoning. The message ID is the durable assistant reply ID for a sessioned request, or [code]-1[/code] for stateless work. Stored history contains visible content, not reasoning.

signal.name: embedding_complete
signal.description: Terminal embedding success carrying a normalized vector. The session is empty for stateless requests. Embedding completion does not add conversation messages.

signal.name: history_truncated
signal.description: Reports stored message IDs omitted while fitting a generation prompt. This is not a terminal signal and does not delete stored history. A later generation error can still occur.

signal.name: generation_error
signal.description: Terminal failure of an accepted generation, embedding, preview or token-count request. The error code uses [enum GodotChorus.ErrorCode], including cancellation. Immediate admission rejections do not emit this signal.

signal.name: engine_failed
signal.description: Reports an engine-wide readiness failure with [constant GodotChorus.ERR_ENGINE_NOT_READY]. This is not a request terminal; each accepted request still receives its own terminal signal.

signal.name: log_record
signal.description: Delivers one structured diagnostic on the host thread. The level uses [enum GodotChorus.LogLevelCode]; fields contain provider-supplied typed values. The request ID is [code]-1[/code] and the session is empty for unowned records. The timestamp is production time in Unix seconds, not delivery time. Logs and inference events use separate queues and have no cross-queue ordering guarantee.
